FACT-1.gloss: Dana has a skip speed of 3 mph

FACT-2.gloss: Dana's skip speed is half the run speed

FACT-4.gloss: Run speed is 4 times the skip speed
FACT-4.verify_reason: Not entailed: problem implies run is 2× skip, not 4× skip.

FACT-6.gloss: Time spent running is 1/3 of total time

FACT-7.gloss: Time spent walking is 2/3 of total time

RULE-1.gloss: If a skip speed is given and half-of-run-speed relation holds and a double relation holds, then the run speed is the doubled value
RULE-1.formula: ∀p∀s∀r((SkipSpeed(p, s) ∧ HalfOfRunSpeed(p) ∧ Double(s, r)) → RunSpeed(p, r))

RULE-2.gloss: If a run speed is known and the run-is-four-times-skip relation holds and skip speed is known and a division relation divides by 4 yields w, then walking speed is w
RULE-2.formula: ∀p∀r∀s∀w((RunSpeed(p, r) ∧ RunIsFourTimesSkip(p) ∧ SkipSpeed(p, s) ∧ Divide(p, r, n_4, w)) → WalkingSpeed(p, w))
RULE-2.verify_reason: Misencoded: uses run-is-four-times-skip and yields walking speed via division by 4, which would correspond to skip, not walking.

RULE-3.gloss: If time spent running is a fraction of total time and total time is known, then running time is the corresponding integer hour
RULE-3.formula: ∀p((TimeSpentRunningIsFraction(p, n_1, n_3) ∧ TotalTime(p, n_6)) → RunningTime(p, n_2))
RULE-3.verify_reason: Not universally valid; running time need not be an integer number of hours.

RULE-4.gloss: If time spent walking is a fraction of total time and total time is known, then walking time is the corresponding hour
RULE-4.formula: ∀p((TimeSpentWalkingIsFraction(p, n_2, n_3) ∧ TotalTime(p, n_6)) → WalkingTime(p, n_4))
RULE-4.verify_reason: Not universally valid; walking time need not be an integer number of hours.

RULE-5.gloss: If running speed and running time are known and a product relation holds, then running distance is given by the product
RULE-5.formula: ∀p∀r∀t∀d((RunSpeed(p, r) ∧ RunningTime(p, t) ∧ Product(p, r, t, d)) → RunningDistance(p, d))

RULE-6.gloss: If walking speed and walking time are known and a product relation holds, then walking distance is given by the product
RULE-6.formula: ∀p∀r∀t∀d((WalkingSpeed(p, r) ∧ WalkingTime(p, t) ∧ Product(p, r, t, d)) → WalkingDistance(p, d))

RULE-7.gloss: If running distance and walking distance are known and their sum is known, then total distance is given
RULE-7.formula: ∀p∀d1∀d2∀d((RunningDistance(p, d1) ∧ WalkingDistance(p, d2) ∧ Sum(p, d1, d2, d)) → TotalDistance(p, d))

INF-1.formula: From FACT-1, FACT-2, FACT-3 by RULE-1 (Modus Ponens)

INF-2.formula: From INF-1, FACT-4, FACT-1, FACT-10 by RULE-2 (Modus Ponens)

INF-3.formula: From FACT-6, FACT-5 by RULE-3 (Universal Instantiation)

INF-4.formula: From FACT-7, FACT-5 by RULE-4 (Universal Instantiation)

INF-5.formula: From INF-1, INF-3, FACT-8 by RULE-5 (Modus Ponens)

INF-6.formula: From INF-2, INF-4, FACT-9 by RULE-6 (Modus Ponens)

INF-7.formula: From INF-5, INF-6, FACT-11 by RULE-7 (Modus Ponens)
